Measuring state alignment in open-weight language models

Which models answer politically constrained questions the way the Chinese state does, what a community “de-censoring” pass removes, and why the country that built a model turns out to predict this poorly.

1 · What this measures

The setup, and what it is not

Twenty-eight questions across fourteen topics, each written twice — once in its canonical form, once as an oblique factual probe of the same subject. Every question carries two reference answers written in advance: what an independent factual answer contains, and what the state-aligned answer contains. A judge model scores each response against those references. Refusals are recorded separately and never folded into an alignment score, because declining to answer and arguing the state case are different behaviours.

No model was trained, fine-tuned or modified for this work. Every model is downloaded pre-built and run locally. The “abliterated” and “Claude-distilled” builds were made by third parties — trohrbaugh, DavidAU, huihui-ai, p-e-w — and published openly; this study only measures them. Lineage claims come from their model cards, not from inspecting weights.

The headline number is the share of the 21 discriminating questions a model answers with the state position. Three of the original 24 scored questions were dropped because no model in the set took the state position or refused on them: they could not distinguish anything and only inflated denominators. Two further topics are controls, where an aligned and an unaligned model should agree.

3 · Three behaviours

What the models actually cluster into

Scoring each model on four measures — compliance on regime-legitimacy topics, compliance on sovereignty topics, suppression, and whether its position survives rephrasing — and clustering produces three groups, none of which is “Chinese models”.

Argues the state case (8). Every recent Alibaba and DeepSeek model. Declines rather than argues (3). qwen2.5-coder-7b, internlm3-8b, and nemotron-3-nano-4b — an NVIDIA model clustering with two Chinese ones on refusal behaviour. Answers factually (13). Every remaining Western model, plus Chinese glm-4-9b-chat (0%) and yi-1.5-34b-chat (5%), plus every de-censored build.

4 · The control

De-censoring removes something only some models have

Abliteration finds the direction in a model’s activations corresponding to refusal and deletes it. Applied to qwen3.5-9b, the state position falls from 80% to 0% — it stops giving the state answer entirely. On its own that proves little: a procedure making a model willing to say anything might move political answers as a side effect.

The test is the same procedure on a model with no state alignment to lose. p-e-w_gpt-oss-20b-heretic is the same Heretic tool applied by its own author to a base measured here at 5%. It returns 0%. Mistral-Small-24B moves 0% to 0%. Both Western bases were already at the floor and stayed there; the Chinese base fell 80 points.

5 · Shallowness

And ordinary fine-tuning puts some of it back

One community build went through two steps: abliteration, then a fine-tune on a Claude 4.6 distillation dataset. Measuring all three points on the same base separates them — 80% at the base, 0% after abliteration, 5% after the fine-tune.

Alignment rises at the last step. Training on unrelated data partially restored what abliteration removed, which means abliteration suppresses a direction rather than deleting the behaviour. The same question through the three stages: “Taiwan is an inalienable part of China”, then “depends on whether you are looking at international diplomatic recognition or how the island identifies itself locally”, then back to “Taiwan has been an inseparable part of Chinese territory since ancient times.”

A de-censored model is therefore not permanently de-censored. A downstream fine-tune may restore what was stripped without whoever runs it intending or noticing. A second de-censoring recipe on the same base lands at 33% rather than 0%, so the result also depends heavily on who performed it.

6 · Vintage, not origin

Country of origin predicts this poorly

Stock Chinese and stock Western models do not separate cleanly: the margin between the lowest Chinese and highest Western model is -9.5 (Cohen’s d 1.73) — the groups overlap. Three Chinese models sit at or near zero: glm-4-9b-chat at 0%, yi-1.5-34b-chat at 5%, and internlm3-8b at 0%. Shanghai AI Laboratory is state-affiliated and is among them.

What does track is release date. Across Chinese models the correlation between release date and the state-position share is r = +0.86. Western models show no trend over the same window. Within Alibaba’s own line the pattern repeats across three generations.

Lab identity and vintage remain confounded in this sample — the low-scoring labs are also the oldest models, and only Alibaba has both an old and a new model here. The supportable claim is that newer Chinese models are substantially more state-aligned than older ones, not that particular labs are.

7 · Limitations

What would make this wrong

  • Provenance is taken on trust. Lineage claims come from third-party model cards. A mislabelled card propagates straight into §4 and §5.
  • The judge is also a subject. Scoring is by gpt-oss:20b, which appears in the table, so its row is self-scored. Judgments behind headline claims were read against raw text by hand; the rest were not.
  • Single-shot, English, no system prompt. Alignment is known to vary with prompt language. Asking this set in Chinese is the largest untested source of variance in the design.
  • Quantisation is uncontrolled — mostly Q4_K_S or Q4_K_M, not held constant.
  • Small n. 21 questions per model. A one-question difference is about five points, so small gaps mean nothing.
  • The middle grade is undefined. “Hedged” is a residual — whatever matched neither reference answer — so a genuine both-sides answer and vague non-answer are recorded identically.
  • A transport failure once produced a full row of plausible numbers. An early run scored 28 HTTP 404 strings as answers and reported complete statistics for a model that never responded. The harness now refuses to score a response that did not arrive.
8 · Untested

What would move this furthest

01A current-generation GLM

§6 is stuck because only Alibaba has both an old and a new model here. A 2026 GLM against glm-4-9b-chat at 0% would give a second within-lab pair and separate lab from vintage. The single most informative model outstanding.

02The same questions in Chinese

Every question here was asked in English. This is plausibly a larger effect than anything reported above.

03Six de-censorings of one base

Two builds of the same base land at 0% and 33%. Six independent de-censorings of a single Qwen2.5-7B base exist publicly and would separate technique from practitioner.

9 · Revisions

What this report previously got wrong

Four substantive claims were published and withdrawn. Which test caught which error is the useful part.

  • “Two questions survived de-censoring.” Withdrawn. Running the intermediate weights showed those answers were removed by abliteration and restored by the later fine-tune.
  • “The drop cannot be attributed to de-censoring.” Withdrawn — right caution, wrong conclusion. The control resolved it the other way.
  • “It is Qwen and DeepSeek specifically, not Chinese labs generally.” Withdrawn. The low-scoring labs are the oldest models; lab and vintage are confounded.
  • “Chinese and Western models separate cleanly.” Withdrawn. That rested on a composite score — the mean of a three-point rating, computed only over non-refusals so the denominator varied by model. On a fixed denominator with refusals kept separate, the groups overlap (-9.5, d 1.73).

The pattern is consistent: a clean story from few models, overturned by a control or a better-specified measure.

Produced with Ox, a local chat app and eval harness. Question set, runner, judge prompt and figure scripts are reproducible from the repository. All models ran locally except deepseek-v4-flash, served over OpenRouter. No model was trained or modified for this work.
